messages:
ops-bot: INCIDENT DETECTED: p99 streaming latency spike > 3s on cluster us-west-2 (auto-alert)
triage-bot: Alert rule: streaming.tail_latency.p99 > 2.5s for 5m. Affected routes: /v1/stream/generate (hosted), model: /redwood/redwood-v2-7b-quant (trt variant)
priya: I'm on it. quick check: is there any deploy in last 30m?
mike: I see a rollout of trt-runtime v8.1.0 yesterday on us-west-2 slot pool A at 02:12 UTC, and a driver bump (nv-520.11) this morning 08:05 UTC. linking deploys: https://infra.internal/deploys/dep-98321
jess: customer impact? any downstream errors in logs?
priya: p95 still mostly ok, p99 jumped from 800ms -> ~3.6s. Streaming stalls (clients see token gaps). Error rate unchanged. No obvious OOMs.
sre-oliver: grabbing node metrics: P95 CPU steady, memory fine. But vmstat shows high page-ins on multiple pods and dmesg has a few lines: "NVRM: GPU fault: GPU access fault on process <decode>"
mike: nvlink errors? can you paste tail -n 100 /var/log/kern.log
sre-oliver: pasted snippet:
```
Mar 12 09:15:42 worker-07 kernel: nvidia: GPU fault on device 0, reason: instr access beyond bounds
Mar 12 09:16:01 worker-12 kernel: nvidia: GPU page fault, migrating pages
Mar 12 09:16:09 worker-12 runtime: flash_attn kernel fallback to reference path
```
priya: interesting — flash_attn fallback + page faults = decode stalls. Did the new trt runtime change kernels used? mike?
mike: TRT 8.1 swapped to a new flash_attn kernel optimized for lane sizes; we have telemetry showing increased compile-time kernel selection changes since the driver bump.
jess: telemetry link: https://telemetry.internal/redwood/runtime/kernels?range=30m (shows spike in "fallback" events)
priya: Plan: 1) triage impact / customers 2) mitigate live (route or rollback) 3) root cause
priya: @oncall-anna can you start customer impact assessment? list top affected orgs and open status page entry if > 3 customers impacted
oncall-anna: starting now — pulling top 20 orgs by error/latency. will DM SRE for direct outreach where needed :phone:
mike: mitigation options: A) rollback trt-runtime to 8.0 on the affected node pool B) force older flash_attn kernel via runtime flag C) route traffic to dedicated fallback pool (no trt) D) full node reboot/driver rollback (painful)
priya: I'd prefer route+force flag while we prepare safe rollback. Can we flip a runtime flag to force "flash_attn=disabled" per-serving-pool?
mike: yes we have config override: runtime.kernel_override.flash_attn = "disabled". Will apply to pool-usw2-a.
priya: do it. mike, also scale up fallback pool by 30% and enable routing policy to prefer fallback when tail_latency > 1s
mike: executing now:
```
# disable kernel (applied to pool-usw2-a)
redwoodctl runtime set-config --pool pool-usw2-a --set "kernel_override.flash_attn=disabled"
# scale fallback
redwoodctl pool scale --name fallback-usw2 --replicas +30%
# update routing
redwoodctl route set-policy --route "/v1/stream/generate" --fallback fallback-usw2 --threshold p95=1s
```
mike: commands returned 200. changes rolling out.
ops-bot: CONFIG CHANGE: kernel_override.flash_attn=disabled applied to pool-usw2-a by mike @ 1748001286
ops-bot: ROUTE UPDATE: /v1/stream/generate fallback->fallback-usw2 threshold p95=1s
jess: monitoring... p99 dropping from 3.6s -> 1.4s now. clients still seeing some hiccups but improved.
priya: good. oncall-anna, update customers: status page draft: "We're investigating increased latency for streaming API in US-West. We've applied mitigations that have reduced tail latency; engineers continue to monitor." I'll publish after you add affected org list.
oncall-anna: published incident note: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-0312-u-s-west-streaming-latency
sre-oliver: logs show remaining kernel fallback events but much lower. I still see occasional GPU page-fault traces on worker-12. Could be a subset of hardware/drivers; I'll isolate nodes with high fault counts and cordon them.
mike: cordoning and shifting traffic off worker-12.. worker-12 drained.
priya: can we reproduce locally by running the decode perf test with trt8.1 + nv-520 on a small harness?
mike: yes, running perf harness with batch sizes and sequence lengths that trigger flash_attn. If I force kernel selection we see a path that calls the new kernel and then a fallback under certain sequence length combos.
jess: reproduction note: sequence len > 1024 + odd batch shapes trigger fallback on some GPUs. That aligns with customer workloads.
priya: root cause hypothesis: new trt8.1 + driver combination triggers an edge-case in flash_attn kernel allocation/IO mapping that causes GPU page faults -> runtime falls back to slower code path -> streaming stalls/tail latency spike.
priya: next steps: 1) create incident ticket and link, 2) schedule rollout rollback of trt-runtime 8.1 to 8.0 for pool-usw2-a (if mitigation not sufficient), 3) long-term: patch kernel or vendor driver, add canary for kernel fallback events
mike: created internal incident #INC-20260312-042. Attaching logs and perf traces.
priya: do we need an immediate rollback? jess: with current routing + flag mitigation p99 down to ~900ms, p95 ~220ms. I'd avoid rollback for now, but keep rollback plan ready in case of regressions.
oncall-anna: SLO update to customers posted. I'm also pinging three top paying customers directly via SEs.
ops-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: Mitigation in place, latency improved. Monitoring for 30m window.
priya: ok handing off to night oncall. next oncall: @sre-oliver will own until 1748002000. Document any regression and escalate if p99 > 1.5s for > 10m.
sre-oliver: acknowledged. I'll keep node cordons and telemetry alerts on. collecting heap/perf dumps and NV logs to attach to the incident.
mike: adding runbook note: add a kernel-fallback alarm to routing so this block can auto-route to fallback pool.
jess: adding a postmortem checklist: reproduce, vendor bug report to Nvidia, kernel patch or runtime workaround, add canary for upcoming trt releases.
priya: thanks team — good triage. If anything spikes again, call it out loudly and we'll escalate to infra+platform. :thumbsup:
oncall-anna: handoff complete. I'll follow up with customer updates in 30m. :bell:
ops-bot: HANDOFF: priya -> sre-oliver @ 1748001350"
